summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and a brief syncopal episode following a polysubstance binge involving cocaine, heroin, and alcohol. He has a significant cardiac history including prior stents and reduced ejection fraction. Evaluation showed no acute heart attack, with normal troponins and EKG changes consistent with prior infarcts. The chest pain and syncope were attributed to demand ischemia likely triggered by cocaine use. Psychiatry evaluated and cleared him, and he was deemed medically stable for discharge. He was counseled on the dangers of substance use, particularly cocaine with his heart condition, and advised to avoid combining metoprolol with cocaine. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his PCP and counselor, though he left without taking discharge paperwork due to attending his nephew’s wake.
